knowledgeAnswers.rationale: The procedure says to match the exact product and formulation to its current SDS, because a similar brand name can carry a different dilution.

The field decision rule says to pause, protect the area and seek supervisor guidance when the answer is unclear. That is the only option that follows it; choosing the product with the client or guessing from the label are not the rule.
The core procedure says to locate product identity, hazard pictograms, directions, first-aid, storage and disposal on the container.

practicalCriteria: Identifies correct product, site-approved use, PPE and emergency information without guessing.
Explains applicable scope and site procedures
Demonstrates hazard controls and safe stop-work decisions
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Assessor observation record covering procedure steps 1-7
stopWorkCriteria: Stop work if procedure step 1 is not done: Read the product identity, hazard pictograms, directions, first-aid, storage and disposal details on the container.
Stop work if procedure step 2 is not done: Match the exact product and formulation to its current safety data sheet (SDS), and do not rely on a similar brand name or a product family.
Stop work if procedure step 3 is not done: Read the SDS sections on hazards, handling, exposure controls, first aid and spills.
